subject: Clarify metering: billable tokens, streaming rounding & commit tier discounts
messages:
From: Jordan Lytle <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@acme-analytics.com
Date: 2026-04-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify metering: billable tokens & commit tiers

Rafael,

Thanks for the pricing deck earlier today — Acme procurement and legal had a few follow-ups around how Redwood defines and bills tokens. We want to make sure the contract language ties to the actual meters so we avoid surprises during usage spikes. Two specific items:

1) Billable tokens definition — does Redwood bill fractional tokens or round per-request? For example, when streaming partial responses, do you charge per emitted token or by some aggregation/window?

2) Rounding & minimal bill increments — we’ve seen vendors round up to the nearest 1k tokens which materially affects small calls. How does Redwood approach rounding for both synchronous generation and streaming (server-push) cases?

Also, we’re evaluating a committed monthly spend with tiered discounts (3T, 10T, 25T monthly token commits). Can you share example math (how rounding and streaming will show up on our invoice) and proposed contract text for the metering section?

We’ve attached a short procurement template for your legal team.

Best,
Jordan Lytle
Director, Procurement | Acme Analytics
procurement@acme-analytics.com

Attachment: procurement_requirements_v1.pdf (attachment referenced in thread)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lytle <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify metering: billable tokens & commit tiers

Jordan — thanks, clear questions. I’ll keep this pragmatic and attach a pricing matrix and SOW draft for the deal. TL;DR answers up front:

- Billable tokens: Redwood bills per emitted token. There are no sub-token fractions on invoices — we round per-request to the nearest whole token. For streaming responses we count each token at emission time; if a single request emits 73.2 token-equivalents in our internal telemetry we bill 74 tokens.

- Rounding policy: rounding is to the nearest whole token per request; we do not aggregate rounding across requests for billing (i.e., we do not batch round-ups into larger buckets by default).

- Commit tiers & discounts: proposed structure below (subject to final approval):
  * Tier A: 3M tokens / month — 5% discount
  * Tier B: 10M tokens / month — 12% discount
  * Tier C: 25M+ tokens / month — 18% discount

Example invoice calculation (Month with streaming-heavy usage):
  - Total emitted tokens (raw telemetry): 11,234,567.9
  - Per-request rounding-produced billed tokens: 11,234,568
  - Committed volume: 10,000,000 (Tier B) => first 10,000,000 billed at discounted rate; overage 1,234,568 billed at standard rate

Draft contract language (suggestion):
  "Billable Tokens" means the number of tokens for which Customer will be billed. Billable Tokens are measured as the count of tokens emitted by the Service in response to Customer requests and are recorded in Redwood’s metering system. All token counts shall be rounded to the nearest whole token per request before aggregation for billing.

  "Streaming Tokens" means tokens emitted as part of a streaming response. Streaming Tokens are counted at emission time and subject to the same rounding rules as synchronous responses.

I’ve attached redwood_v1_pricing_matrix.csv (shows per-token price and discount schedule) and a SOW draft that references measurement windows and invoice examples. Neha — can you and legal review the suggested wording and confirm whether we should allow an alternate rounding aggregation for large-volume customers? Marissa — can you confirm discount authority on the tiers above?

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Attachment: redwood_v1_pricing_matrix.csv, SOW_draft_Acme.docx

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Jordan Lytle <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-23T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify metering: billable tokens & commit tiers

Adding a couple operational clarifications from sales ops/legal side:

1) Measurement window — Redwood aggregates per-request rounded counts into a monthly invoice period (UTC). If Acme wants invoices aligned to a different timezone or custom billing cycle, we can support that as part of the SOW.

2) Rounding edge-case for streaming — for very chatty streaming sessions there is noise from intermittent ACKs and heartbeats. To avoid billing noise, we can offer an optional 5-token per-request floor for streaming responses (i.e., any streaming response that would round to fewer than 5 tokens is billed at 5 tokens). This is optional and typically applies when customers have a lot of <10-token keep-alives.

3) Aggregated rounding alternative — for customers who do lots of tiny calls (high frequency, small payloads) we can offer an aggregation mode where rounding is applied after summing raw tokens across all requests in the invoice period (reduces rounding inflation). This mode requires an explicit contract clause and is available for Tier B/C customers.

Suggested legal tweak to the "Billable Tokens" clause to match ops:
  "Billable Tokens" are measured by Redwood’s metering system and rounded to the nearest whole token per request unless Customer has contracted an aggregated-rounding billing mode. Streaming responses that would round to fewer than five (5) tokens may be subject to a minimum charge of five (5) tokens per streaming response when the optional streaming floor is enabled.

Jordan — if Acme is comfortable with the aggregation option for Tier B/C customers, that will reduce the effective rounding overhead. If not, the per-request rounding is our default.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Jordan Lytle <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-04-24T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify metering: billable tokens & commit tiers

Looping in final commercial approval. Rafael/Neha — approved subject to two adjustments:

1) Increase Tier C discount to 20% (on the condition of an annual committed contract and quarterly usage reviews).
2) Approve aggregated-rounding mode for Tier B and C as a contract option (must be opted-in and cannot be changed mid-term).

Also: offer Acme one month of onboarding credit equal to 100% of the Tier A commit to offset migration/testing (applied as invoice credit). We will include explicit examples in the SOW showing how aggregation affects a high-frequency small-call workload.

Jordan — if that works we’ll update the SOW and push a DocuSign envelope with the commit tiers and the agreed metering language.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Jordan Lytle <procurement@acme-analytics.com>

Date: 2026-04-24T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify metering: billable tokens & commit tiers

Marissa/Team — thanks, that sounds reasonable. Acme accepts:
  - Tier A: 3M (5%)
  - Tier B: 10M (12%) with aggregation option (we opt in)
  - Tier C: 25M+ (20%) with quarterly reviews and annual commitment
  - Optional 5-token streaming floor: not required for us; we’ll keep it disabled for now
  - Please include the invoice examples and aggregation math in the SOW.

Next steps: please send the updated SOW and DocuSign link and we’ll route to legal for a fast review.

Jordan Lytle
